title: A Kitchen for the Orchard
premise: Ada Vane has spent ten years ghostwriting other people's lives while burying his own, including the confession he owes his estranged sister before her orchard estate is sold. When his publisher assigns him to ghostwrite the memoirs of celebrated romance author Marguerite Hale—his sister's oldest friend and his own long-ago love—he agrees to pose as her date for the Hale family reunion, a fiction that curdles into something true by the dessert course. As Marguerite's dictated chapters begin echoing Ada's own buried past, he realizes she has known who he was all along and hired him as a final test of loyalty. At the orchard's last harvest, Ada must choose between delivering the manuscript that will save his career and speaking the decade-old sentence that will cost him everything but himself.
about_author: Edmund Ravensworth is the pen name of a former orchard hand turned literary ghostwriter who spent a decade writing love stories he never believed he deserved. He lives within sight of an apple orchard and insists, in interviews he never gives, that every confession in his fiction is true.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In a rented flat above a bakery, Ada finishes ghostwriting a footballer's memoir and rehearses, as he does every year on the same date, the sentence he has never said aloud. His agent calls: the Marguerite Hale job, double his fee, deadline brutal. He accepts for the money he needs to delay his sister's orchard sale. Beat: disciplined self-erasure established.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. First meeting with Marguerite at her townhouse: she is sharper and wearier than her books suggest, and she proposes an unusual clause—he will accompany her to the Hale family reunion as her 'colleague' to deflect her family's marriage interrogations. Ada recognizes the surname Hale from his sister's letters and hesitates; Marguerite watches him hesitate. Beat: the trap closes gently.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over interview sessions, Marguerite dictates a romance about a woman who once loved a boy in an orchard, and Ada transcribes details only two people alive could know. Meanwhile Marguerite coaches him on their fake-relationship backstory, and their rehearsals grow uncomfortably convincing. Beat: the past leaks into the present through fiction.

chapters.title: The Reunion
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Hale estate reunion: Ada performs the devoted colleague, deflecting a predatory uncle and Marguerite's probing mother, until a game of 'how we met' forces him to improvise a story that is, word for word, the truth of a night neither of them has ever mentioned. By dessert, the performance has stopped being one. Beat: the fake becomes real.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, revealed for the first time. She rereads Ada's transcript and finds him annotating her dictated chapters with corrections that reveal he remembers everything—the orchard, the promise, the night he vanished. We learn she hired him deliberately, testing whether the boy who abandoned her sister and her has become a man who stays. Beat: her wound and her scheme surface.

chapters.title: The Sister's Orchard
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada visits his sister Iris at the failing orchard, intending to deliver the money and finally the sentence, but Iris, sharp with illness and grief, tells him Marguerite wrote to her years ago asking why he left. Ada realizes the two women have compared notes, and that his silence has been a debt accruing interest for a decade. Beat: loyalty and truth collide.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The manuscript nears completion, and Marguerite dictates its final chapter: the heroine waiting in an orchard for a confession that never comes. Ada, recognizing the ending as an accusation, begs her to change it; she refuses, saying endings must be earned, not edited. The sale of Iris's orchard is finalized for the same week as the book's delivery. Beat: pressure from every side.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Wrote
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite discovers Ada has secretly rewritten her ending—giving the heroine the confession, in his own voice, signed not with his pen name but with the boy's real name. Furious and undone, she confronts him: he has used her book to say the sentence, hiding even his honesty inside someone else's pages. Beat: climax of exposure; love declared and rejected as cowardice.

chapters.title: The Last Harvest
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the orchard's final day before sale, Ada arrives without manuscript, without fee, without fiction, and says the rehearsed sentence aloud to Iris and Marguerite together—apologizing for the night he ran, naming what he felt, asking for nothing. Marguerite walks away without answering, and Ada stays to help pick the last apples anyway. Beat: the price paid; love offered without terms.

chapters.title: A Kitchen for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, then shared. Months later, Marguerite's memoir publishes with a new final chapter she wrote herself: the confession, accepted. She finds Ada restoring the orchard's old kitchen as a gift to Iris, having bought the land with the fee he never cashed. She hands him a pen and a blank page—his own, this time. Beat: resolution; love chosen over both duty and survival.
